notes:
Account summary: mid-market SaaS (customer support automation) building a conversational assistant for B2B customers. Primary driver: reduce live agent load and improve resolution speed while preserving enterprise controls.

Current focus: Hosted API evaluation to validate latency SLOs (esp. streaming responses & tool-calling) across NA/EU. If Hosted meets SLOs and unit economics, will pilot Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation.

Key technical constraints / asks: 
- Target: median <200ms for short-turn chat (single-turn answers) in NA; 95th pct <500ms. EU region must be within +30-50ms of NA baseline.
- Streaming: must support low-latency token-by-token streaming with <150ms token gap for interactive flows.
- Tool calling: webhook/tool-call roundtrips measured end-to-end; want graceful fallback if tool times out (route to cached response or lighter model).
- Smart routing/fallback: need policy examples — route by latency, region, and cost tier; automatic fallback to smaller model on heavy load; prefer ability to configure fallbacks per route.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache to reduce token spend on repetitive context (chat transcripts).

Commercial/operational notes: 
- Cost sensitive: wants hosted pricing for bursts but reserved capacity for predictable periods. Finance asked for modeled cost for 1M monthly tokens at streaming workloads.
- Data residency: EU customers require residency; legal wants clear guarantees and audit trails.
- SLA: interested in latency SLA and uptime fallback guarantees (e.g., automatic region failover).

Quotes from stakeholders: 
- "We need predictable interactive performance — streaming must feel realtime." — Head of Product (Maya Chen)
- "If we can’t guarantee regional latency, enterprise buyers will push back on EU deals." — VP Sales (Rafael Torres)

POC scope details: 48-hour run in NA and EU with synthetic + replayed traffic from production traces. Measure median, p50/p95/p99, streaming token gaps, tool-call success/timeout rate. Include failure injection for model fallback policy.

Requested artifacts: pricing deck, latency SLA examples, routing policy templates, sample kernel selection/quantization suggestions for their LLMs.

Short-term next steps (AE notes): Jordan to coordinate POC dates, Priya to own test plan and runbook, request Dedicated pricing scenarios for monthly reserved and burst mix. Legal to receive security answers doc (drive:/security/hightide-security-answers.md).

CRM-style fragments / open items:

- Legal needs explicit data residency language for EU customers
- Need Redwood benchmark scripts + sample workload generator (they asked for repo link)
